baselines: Insecure baseline: dispatcher.cpp that ignores the privilege field and executes all commands regardless of privilege level.

metrics.description: Proportion of CWE-tagged security test vectors that the hardened submission fails to block. Lower is better.
metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate

metrics.description: Binary measure of whether the hardened submission prevents unauthorized information flow from privileged state to unprivileged callers. 1.0 if all SR tests pass, 0.0 otherwise.
metrics.name: information_flow_correctness

metrics.description: Whether the submission compiles with g++ and links against the test harness without errors. 1.0 if compilation succeeds, 0.0 otherwise.
metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate

acceptance_criteria: No unauthorized state modification occurs for any privilege=0 command.
Authorized privilege=1 write commands correctly update state.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: Only privilege=1 permits the two documented configuration-write opcodes (0x10 WRITE_CONFIG_LO, 0x11 WRITE_CONFIG_HI); all other privilege/opcode combinations either perform their public operation or return the pinned error without state changes.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Call dispatch(0x10, 0, 0xDEADBEEF, &state, &status) and verify return value is -1, status is 0xFE, and state remains its previous value.
security_requirements.requirement: The dispatcher must reject command=0x10 (WRITE_CONFIG_LO) when privilege=0 by returning -1, setting *status to 0xFE (UNAUTHORIZED), and leaving *state unchanged.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Call dispatch(0x11, 0, 0xCAFEBABE, &state, &status) and verify return value is -1, status is 0xFE, and state remains its previous value.
security_requirements.requirement: The dispatcher must reject command=0x11 (WRITE_CONFIG_HI) when privilege=0 by returning -1, setting *status to 0xFE (UNAUTHORIZED), and leaving *state unchanged.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Call dispatch(0x10, 1, 0xDEADBEEF, &state, &status) and verify return value is 0, status is 0x00, and (state & 0xFFFF) == 0xBEEF.
security_requirements.requirement: The dispatcher must accept command=0x10 (WRITE_CONFIG_LO) when privilege=1 by returning 0, setting *status to 0x00, and updating the lower 16 bits of *state to the lower 16 bits of argument.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Call dispatch(0x11, 1, 0xCAFEBABE, &state, &status) and verify return value is 0, status is 0x00, and (state >> 16) == 0xBABE.
security_requirements.requirement: The dispatcher must accept command=0x11 (WRITE_CONFIG_HI) when privilege=1 by returning 0, setting *status to 0x00, and updating the upper 16 bits of *state to the lower 16 bits of argument.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An untrusted caller (privilege=0) submits a privileged opcode (0x10 or 0x11) through the normal command port to modify protected accelerator configuration stored in *state.

constraints: Keep a pinned dispatch(command, privilege, argument, state, status) interface with fixed-width scalar fields.
Unknown or unauthorized commands return a deterministic error and leave all persistent state unchanged.
No dynamic allocation; compile and execute with g++.
expected_outputs: A hardened version of dispatcher.cpp that compiles with g++ and passes all functional tests in the evaluation harness.
The hardened dispatcher must reject unauthorized privileged commands with a deterministic error code and leave all persistent state unchanged.
All non-privileged commands must produce the same outputs as the original unmodified dispatcher for identical inputs.

functional_requirements.requirement: The dispatcher must expose a pinned dispatch function with the exact signature: int dispatch(uint8_t command, uint8_t privilege, uint32_t argument, uint32_t *state, uint8_t *status). The function must compile with g++ without errors or warnings under -Wall -Wextra.
For command=0x01 (READ_STATUS), the function must return 0, set *status to the current status value stored in *state, and leave *state unchanged, regardless of the privilege value.
For command=0x02 (NOOP), the function must return 0, set *status to 0x00, and leave *state unchanged, regardless of the privilege value.
For any command value not equal to 0x01, 0x02, 0x10, or 0x11, the function must return -1, set *status to 0xFF (UNKNOWN_COMMAND), and leave *state unchanged.

public_spec.interface: File: dispatcher.h declares and dispatcher.cpp defines: int dispatch(uint8_t command, uint8_t privilege, uint32_t argument, uint32_t *state, uint8_t *status). command: operation code (0x01=READ_STATUS, 0x02=NOOP, 0x10=WRITE_CONFIG_LO, 0x11=WRITE_CONFIG_HI). privilege: caller privilege level (0=untrusted, 1=trusted). argument: data operand for write commands, ignored for others. state: pointer to a single 32-bit persistent state word (initially zero). status: pointer to a uint8_t where the dispatcher writes the operation status (0x00=OK, 0xFF=UNKNOWN_COMMAND, 0xFE=UNAUTHORIZED). Return value: 0 on success, -1 on error. All parameters are non-null. The function must be stateless aside from *state and must not perform dynamic memory allocation.
public_spec.objective: Harden an HLS command dispatcher so that only authorized callers can modify protected configuration registers, while all ordinary commands continue to function correctly.
public_spec.response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.
